risks: Minimal physical risk. The main risks are that residents fear consequences for criticising the programme, that assessors feel judged, and that small groups make individuals identifiable in quotations.
consent: Written informed consent before each interview and focus group, taken by the research assistant; participants may withdraw until analysis begins, and declining has no effect on assessments or progression.
data: Audio recordings deleted after verified transcription; transcripts de-identified (names, rotations, dates removed) and stored on the university research drive with access limited to the two analysts; quotations checked for identifiability before any report.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: residents who are international medical graduates, those with caring responsibilities, part-time residents and residents with low assessment counts may experience the target differently and may be least likely to volunteer. Invitations are made through the residents' association as well as the department office, sampling is purposive across these groups, and the report states which groups are thinly represented.
effectiveness: The study is useful if it gives the committee reasons and mechanisms it can act on in June; it will not claim that any change to the target works.
efficiency: Uses existing research assistant time and approved half-days; interviews in lunch hours avoid lost clinical time.
costs: Staff time only: about 180 hours of research assistant time and 40 hours of analyst time; no transcription service fee because transcription is done in house.
grants: None needed; a departmental education research award could fund dissemination to other programmes.
partnerships: Residents' association (recruitment and guide review), a faculty assessor representative, the chief residents, and the programme administrators.
rebPath: Approved by the hospital research ethics board as minimal-risk research (approval REB-2026-0412, 2026-09-03). Any change to the interview guide beyond probes is submitted as an amendment.
limitations: One programme; findings are transferable by description, not generalisable by sampling; participants may shape accounts for an audience that includes their programme.
summary: Minimal-risk study with written consent, an independent interviewer, de-identified transcripts and purposive sampling of residents least likely to volunteer.
